'''Gerhard Lagaly''' (born 14 October 1938, in [[Ludwigshafen am Rhein]]) is a German chemist and retired university professor.

==Life and work==

In 1957, Lagaly started his studies in Chemistry (as well as in Physics, [[Mineralogy]] and Botany) at the [[Heidelberg University]], receiving his degree as "''Diplom-Chemiker''" in 1962. He conducted his doctorate studies at the Institute for Inorganic Chemistry at the same institution under [[Armin Weiss]], and was awarded his Doctor degree in 1967 with the work "''Untersuchung von Quellungsvorgängen in n-Alkylammonium-Schichtsilicaten''". From 1965, he worked as an assistant at the Institute for Inorganic Chemistry of [[LMU Munich]] where he concluded his [[Habilitation]] in 1971 and then was employed as lecturer ("''Akademischer Rat/Oberrat''"). In 1974, he was employed as Professor for Inorganic Chemistry at [[Kiel University]], retiring in 2004.

His research lines concentrated on [[Clay chemistry]], [[Colloid]] chemistry and [[Interface and colloid science|Interface]] chemistry as well as chemistry from porous compounds, layered materials and [[Intercalation (chemistry)|intercalation chemistry]].

Among his many contributions to the fields of [[clay]] and [[colloid chemistry]], one of his most recognized developments was the ''Alkylammonium Method'' for the determination of [[Surface charge|layer charge]] in layered aluminosilicates.<ref>Lagaly, G. and Weiss, A. (1969) Determination of the layer
charge in mica-type layer silicates: in Proc. lnt. Clay Conf.,
Tokyo, 1969, Vol. 1, L. Heller, ed., Israel University Press,
Jerusalem, 61–80.</ref>

He acted as treasurer of the German Colloid Society from 1979 to 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kolloid-gesellschaft.de/index.php/en/about-us/history|title=History|website=Kolloid-gesellschaft.de|access-date=2016-01-08|archive-date=2016-01-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126212246/http://www.kolloid-gesellschaft.de/index.php/en/about-us/history|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004 the same institution awarded him with the Wolfgang Ostwald Prize.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kolloid-gesellschaft.de/index.php/en/awards/ostwald-prize|title=Ostwald Prize|website=Kolloid-gesellschaft.de|access-date=2016-01-08|archive-date=2018-01-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127143225/http://www.kolloid-gesellschaft.de/index.php/en/awards/ostwald-prize|url-status=dead}}</ref> Lagaly was President of the German Clay Group (DTTG) from 1987 to 1992 and of the European Clay Groups Association (ECGA) from 1999 to 2003.

In addition, Lagaly acted for many years (1987–2004) as editor-in-chief for "Colloid and Polymer Science"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/396|title=Colloid and Polymer Science|website=Springer.com}}</ref> and "Progress Colloid and Polymer Science"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/series/2882|title=Progress in Colloid and Polymer Science|website=Springer.com}}</ref> as well as editor for "Clay Minerals"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/claymin|title=Clay Minerals &#124; GeoScienceWorld|website=Pubs.geoscienceworld.org}}</ref> (1982–1996) and "Applied Clay Science"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/applied-clay-science/|title=Applied Clay Science &#124; Journal &#124; ScienceDirect.com by Elsevier|website=Journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> (1985–1996).

==The Gerhard Lagaly Award==
The German Clay Group (DTTG)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dttg.ethz.ch/dttgaufgabe_en.html|title=Purpose of the DTTG|website=Dttg.ethz.ch}}</ref> awards the Gerhard Lagaly Award, to "''internationally excellent scientists with outstanding original research in the field of clay mineralogy.''" 
''The award is designated after the internationally highly recognized clay scientist and the distinguished member of the DTTG, Professor Dr. Dr. Gerhard Lagaly.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dttg.ethz.ch/dttgpreise_en.html|title=Preis der DTTG|website=Dttg.ethz.ch}}</ref>

The prize was first awarded in 2014 to Prof. Dr. Juraj Bujdák (Comenius University Bratislava). In 2016, the prize went to Dr. habil. Sabine Petit (Université de Poitiers). The recipient of the 2018 prize was Dr. Stephan Kaufhold (BGR Hannover).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dttg.ethz.ch/dttgpreise_lagaly_en.html|title=DTTG Awards|website=Dttg.ethz.ch}}</ref>

==Lagalyite==
In March 2017 a hydrated calcium phyllomanganate with formula Ca<sub>2x</sub>Mn<sub>1−x</sub>O<sub>2</sub>•1.5-2H<sub>2</sub>O (x = 0.05–0.08) was accepted as new mineral by the [[International Mineralogical Association]]. This new species was discovered and described by [[:de:Thomas Witzke|Dr. Thomas Witzke]] and colleagues. It was named [[Lagalyite]], in honor of Gerhad Lagaly and his contributions to the fields of clay chemistry and mineralogy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://minmag.geoscienceworld.org/content/gsminmag/81/2/403.full.pdf|title=Mineralogical Magazine, April 2017, Vol. 81(2), pp. 403–409|website=Minmag.geoscienceworld.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mindat.org/min-51579.html|title=Lagalyite: Lagalyite mineral information and data.|website=Mindat.org}}</ref>
